items.title: Can Home Depot Reignite Growth Amid Weak Big-Ticket Demand?
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q3 sales growth of 4.9% to $43.4B with 2.2% comparable sales growth, driven by online strength (13% comps) and professional customer gains. However, big-ticket demand remains uneven, and margin pressures persist. The company projects 1.4% comps growth for fiscal 2026. Similar challenges affect competitors Lowe's and Williams-Sonoma, though the latter shows resilience in furniture sales.

items.title: Home Depot Just Delivered Great News to Investors
items.summary: Home Depot reported its strongest same-store sales growth since Q3 2022 at 2.2%, driven by higher average ticket sizes and strength in power and appliances. CFO Richard McPhail will become CEO while Ted Decker transitions to chairman. The company raised full-year guidance for sales growth to 4.5% and same-store sales growth to 1.4%, though the home improvement environment remains challenging due to past COVID-driven demand pull-forward and elevated interest rates.

items.title: Home Depot Q3 Earnings Call Flags Margin Pressure as Sales Grow
items.summary: Home Depot lowered its fiscal 2026 sales growth guidance to 4.5% and adjusted operating margin to approximately 12.8%, citing a softer-than-expected home improvement market. The company reported Q3 comparable sales growth of 2.2% driven by smaller repair jobs, with sales of $43.40B topping estimates. Incoming CEO Richard McPhail attributed the margin pressure to lower-margin product categories and SRS acquisition mix shifts, while also trimming SRS organic growth outlook to low single digits due to weak roofing demand.

items.title: Home Depot’s Comparable Sales Rose 2.2% Even as Customer Transactions Fell 0.5%. Here’s What’s Behind the Gap.
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q3 2026 earnings that narrowly beat consensus estimates with $43.4B in sales (up 5% YoY) and comparable sales growth of 2.2%, despite a 0.5% decline in customer transactions. The gap was explained by a 3% increase in average ticket size, driven by strength in the B2B Pro division and categories like appliances and power tools. The company announced three C-suite leadership changes and narrowed full-year guidance on operating margins and EPS growth, which weighed on stock sentiment.

items.title: Home Depot Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates, Sales Beat on Comps Growth
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q3 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.86, meeting estimates, with sales growing 4.9% to $43.4 billion. Comparable sales rose 2.2% driven by higher average ticket ($93.09), though customer transactions declined slightly. However, gross margin contracted 60 basis points to 32.8% due to cost of sales outpacing revenue growth. Operating margin also narrowed 30 basis points. Management updated FY26 guidance projecting 4.5% sales growth and 1.4% comparable sales growth.

items.title: Home Depot's Best Comp of the Year Arrives With a Thinner Margin
items.summary: Home Depot exceeded Q3 revenue expectations with $43.4B in sales (up 4.9%) and 2.2% comparable sales growth, but margins contracted significantly. Gross margin fell to 32.8% from 33.4% year-over-year, with the company guiding sales to the high end while margins move to the low end of guidance. The margin pressure stems from acquisition-driven growth through lower-margin professional distribution channels. Management also implied fourth-quarter comparable sales will decelerate to around 1% despite strong current momentum.

items.summary: Home Depot is expected to report Q3 fiscal 2026 results on November 17 with projected revenue growth of 3.3% to $42.7B and EPS growth of 3.5%. While the company benefits from strong Pro sales, digital expansion, and smaller home improvement projects, near-term challenges include weak housing turnover, margin pressures from tariffs and operating costs, and a premium valuation of 22.27X forward P/E.

items.title: Can Home Depot Sustain Comparable Sales Growth Amid Uneven Demand?
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q2'26 comparable sales growth of 1.7% year-over-year, driven by professional customer demand and 11% digital sales growth across 13 of 16 departments. However, comparable transactions declined 1%, indicating ticket-driven rather than volume-led growth. The company reaffirmed flat to 2% comps guidance for FY26 as persistent housing affordability pressures and consumer uncertainty continue to constrain larger discretionary renovation projects.

items.title: Home Depot's Margin Outlook Faces Inflationary Headwinds
items.summary: Home Depot's Q2 gross margin expanded 25 bps to 33.7%, boosted by $685M in tariff refunds, but underlying profitability faces headwinds from rising fuel, energy, and input costs, plus acquisition-related mix pressures totaling 120 bps. Management expects these cost increases to offset tariff benefits throughout fiscal 2026, with peers Lowe's and Williams-Sonoma experiencing similar margin compression from inflationary pressures.

items.title: Are Smaller Home Projects Sustaining Home Depot's Sales Growth?
items.summary: Home Depot reported Q2'26 comparable sales growth of 1.7% driven by resilient demand for repair and maintenance projects, with digital sales climbing 11%. However, underlying demand remains uneven as transactions declined 1% while average ticket grew 2.8%, indicating consumers are spending more per visit but visiting less frequently. Management reaffirmed flat to 2% FY26 comps guidance. Lowe's and Williams-Sonoma are also benefiting from similar small-project spending trends, though with varying momentum.

items.title: Home Depot vs. Target: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Home Depot and Target as retail investment options for 2026. While Home Depot demonstrates stronger financials with $164.7B revenue and 8.6% net margin, Target is recommended as the better buy due to its lower valuation (P/E 14.6x vs 21.3x), new CEO Michael Fiddelke's $5B transformation initiative showing strong early results (6% sales growth, 35% profit increase in H1 2026), and higher dividend yield of 3.1%. Both stocks face distinct risks including macroeconomic headwinds for Home Depot and operational challenges for Target.

items.title: This Homebuilder's Average Selling Price Just Hit a 9-Year Low. Here's Why That's Great News for Home Depot

Despite short-term economic concerns, Home Depot's stock trades at an attractive valuation with positive long-term outlook.
